2611.30188.abstract_source_note: Official New abstract preserves unresolved oursfull/ours macros and ends before the extra quantitative results in the PDF abstract. Full official New wording is retained. Official PDF resolves the method name as Judgment-in-the-Loop (JiL).

2611.31053.metadata_source_note: Project and repository list additional authors and Maniformer compared with the official New/PDF author block. This digest preserves official authors and the four PDF affiliations; it does not silently merge versions.

2611.28324.image_caption: Figure 1: The MatHarness ideation-to-paper cycle: a round table produces an executable experiment plan, the Researcher executes it under just-in-time auditing, and the writing agent synthesizes and audits the scientific story, triggering follow-up cycles (Appendix C ).

2611.28574.image_caption: Figure 1 : EvoViM evolves task-specific visual programs from one generic starting program. Each panel shows an evolved program on a held-out episode, with the evolved mechanisms named in its header. Red marks the evidence the program finds or the action it suggests.

2611.29613.image_caption: Figure 3. Effects of direct edits. (a) Dev-day query-tower effects and the distribution of 1,258 edits across both towers. (b) LayerNorm gain scaling. (c) Branch, offset and shortcut scaling. (d) L0 shortcut token shares before and after mixing search. Four panels show single-edit effects, normalization gain scaling, branch and offset scaling, and token shares before and after search.

2611.30011.image_caption: Figure 5 : Memory of the final harness at question time on three OVO-Bench test questions (tasks EPM, ASI, and FPD). Questions and options are reproduced verbatim. Each panel gives the question, its options (green: correct; red: the seed’s choice), and both answers with the probability P ⁡ ( gold ) P(\text{gold}) of the correct option. The timeline shows what the write path stored from the start of the video to the question (black marker). Notes : captions every 16 s, chapter notes over four captions, and a step log of who does what (purple outline: steps cited in the answer prompt). Index : ViCLIP vectors of 16-s segments and 4-frame windows, darker when closer to the question and options. Frames : the 64-frame store (tall ticks: segment key frames; pale ticks: frames since forgotten). Tools : OWLv2 detections, dark if the noun is named in the question or options. Read : the frames sent to the VLM, retrieved key frames in purple and the 4 most recent frames in gray. Thumbnails show six of them with the selector that chose each: similarity to the question ( CLIP , ViCLIP index ), temporal coverage ( recency , gap fill , caption gap ), or the last strong scene change ( visual change ). The seed sends only the captions and the 4 most recent frames.

2611.30101.image_caption: Figure 1: Overview of AoG. (a) A planner coordinates agent reasoning with ongoing observation and frozen-policy execution under physical time constraints. Three coupled inner loops refine intervention timing, recovery programs, and policy resumption. Across RSI rounds, the agent revises planner guidance and inner-loop rules and programs from complete trajectories; subsequent executions use the updated harness. (b) Online execution efficiency on RoboDojo-Sim, comparing AoG with agentic baselines in terms of token consumption and end-to-end latency per episode. Both metrics measure deployment costs, excluding RSI training costs. (c) Success rate and score across five task categories on RoboDojo-Sim, comparing AoG with policy-only and agentic baselines.

2611.30139.image_caption: Fig. 3: TSP benchmark mean gap of each round’s candidate solver. The curves include rejected candidates and show candidate performance rather than the sequence of retained skills.

2611.30424.image_caption: Figure 1 : Overview of Spatial-Zero. (a) Self-generated, geometry-verified spatial experiences improve spatial reasoning. (b) Comparison of learning paradigms in data dependence, scene generation, and ground-truth supervision. (c) MMSI improvements across three backbones.

2611.30671.image_caption: Figure 1: Target adaptation and strategy refinement in DriveDreamer-RSI. (a) Prior work. Controllable driving generators use scene conditions to produce training data for perception models. (b) Gap-Guided Target Adaptation. The perception model’s current capability gaps determine the next generation targets. (c) Learning-Feedback-Driven Strategy Refinement. The agent draws on past experience stored in memory to refine its data construction strategy.

2611.31048.image_caption: Figure 3 : Overview of Hindsight Twins (HinT). (1) On a failed student rollout, the critic reports the intended fix f f ( Fix ), the observed error a a ( Seen ), and a slotted revision template T T . (2) Filling T T gives r = T ⁡ ( f ) r=T(f) and its twin r ~ = T ⁡ ( a ) \tilde{r}=T(a) , which differ only in the slot; their token states are aligned outside it as described in Sec. 3.3 . (3) At a shared re-noised latent ( x σ , σ ) (x_{\sigma},\sigma) , the round-start teacher θ ¯ \bar{\theta} adds the twin velocity difference, scaled by λ ​ w ​ ( σ ) \lambda w(\sigma) , to its original-prompt anchor (the thought bubbles illustrate the two conditions, not sampled images). (4) Only the student’s LoRA weights are trained toward this detached target under c c via Eq. 3 , and the teacher is refreshed from the student every round. Photographs: Qwen-Image-2512 before and after four HinT rounds under the sunset-favoring critic (same prompt and seed).

2611.29062.image_caption: Figure 7: Harness construction, recommendation traces, and aggregate results for two unseen PersonaMemv3 users.

2611.29619.image_caption: Figure 2: The Wiring view during a run of the demonstration on Wactorz 0.8, grouped by machine. Agents are on the left of each band and topics are rounded boxes. The detector on the main machine publishes person-detection , which feeds a lamp trigger on main and a counter that has been migrated to the rpi-kitchen node: the edge crosses machines because the counter subscribes to a topic, not to an agent. The trigger’s output topic is outlined in red because no agent reads it; a topic only the dashboard reads is marked as such rather than as a problem.

2611.30287.image_caption: Figure 1 : Motivation and overview of MMMem. (a) Without task-level memory, the evidence for a question stays scattered across records, and the agent can repeat mistakes on related questions. (b) MMMem organizes multimodal memory, generates tasks for warm-up and training, turns solved tasks into experiences, and retrieves and reuses them on later tasks.

2611.31160.image_caption: Figure 1: Habitats evolutionary lifecycle. At generation t t , the population 𝒫 t \mathcal{P}_{t} contains executable reward–policy pairs. (1) Policies for newly synthesized rewards are trained from scratch, while inherited survivor policies remain fixed. (2) Every policy is evaluated under every population reward to construct the cross-fitness matrix 𝐅 t \mathbf{F}_{t} . (3) Normalized cross-fitness profiles are used to compute Specialist Quality (SQ), Behavioral Diversity (BD), and Grounded Behavioral Profile Coverage (GC). (4) Individuals whose policies dominate their own reward niches and outperform the random-policy baseline form the survivor set 𝒱 t \mathcal{V}_{t} . (5) The Planner determines the offspring count, selects parents, and proposes mutation directives, while the Mutator generates and validates executable reward programs. Valid offspring join the survivors to form 𝒫 t + 1 = 𝒱 t ∪ 𝒪 t \mathcal{P}_{t+1}=\mathcal{V}_{t}\cup\mathcal{O}_{t} ; invalid candidates receive up to three replacement attempts before their offspring slot is discarded.

2611.28287.image_caption: Figure 6: A truth-switch pair. The two witness videos share the initial reveal and the covered final frame and differ only in their events, so V 0 V_{0} realizes C 0 C_{0} and V 1 V_{1} realizes C 1 C_{1} . Both candidate trajectories are shown with each video, in both orders.

2611.28781.image_caption: Figure 1 : The setting. A vision model has been moved into a new system and may carry a fault in the images it receives, in its stored weights, or in the way its outputs are read. An agent that can read the weights and run a limited number of forward passes gives a verdict, a diagnosis and an additive edit of the weights. Right: outputs of three deployed models before and after the agent’s edit (a rotated input in classification, flipped kernels in segmentation, a wrong box-coordinate order in detection; examples from Figure 3 ).

2611.29290.image_caption: Figure 2: The matched factorial design. Each comparison changes one axis (model, skill, harness, or budget) on the same task instances and holds the others fixed.

2611.29306.image_caption: Figure 1: Motivation and overview of DoppelVet. a , Verifier-equivalent updates can have different safety outcomes. b , DoppelVet compares matched executions before persistence. c , This improves harmful-update detection, long-term stability, and tool-use safety.

2611.29651.image_caption: Figure 2: Judge audit. Each cell is the percentage of 471 math problems on which a judge accepts a family’s seeding string as a correct answer. Families are ordered by mean FPR over the four core judges. xVerify accepts no string on more than 0.4% of problems, and the held-out Qwen3.6-35B-A3B accepts essentially one string.

2611.30897.image_caption: Fig. 1: Overview of the decoupled single-generation forecasting and validation workflow. 1. Nested Regions & Pilots: Perturbation drives net inflow from common region A c A^{c} across x 1 = 0 x_{1}=0 into periphery A ∖ B A\setminus B , while driving net outflow from core B B (solid ring; inner ellipse I I dotted). Short pilot chains record outputs at rounds 0 , 1 , 3 , 5 0,1,3,5 . The quota strip ( m = 40 m=40 , quarter-row setting, 40 : 66 : 22 40:66:22 ) shows fresh real (grey, m m ), clean synthetic (teal, s − u s-u ), and perturbed synthetic (plum, u u ) rows. 2. Single-Gen Calibration: Saved anchor runs are reweighted and split by source counts ( k 1 , k 2 , k 3 ) (k_{1},k_{2},k_{3}) to train independent one-step models. Three mini-plots summarize the resulting outputs: teal clean g ⁡ ( D ) g(D) and plum perturbed g σ ​ ( D ) g^{\sigma}(D) shares across ( A c , A ∖ B , B ) (A^{c},A\setminus B,B) (Fashion-MNIST, m = 72 m=72 , σ = 0.75 \sigma=0.75 ), and orange binned failure rates h ^ \widehat{h} . Convex interpolation across anchors supplies responses for any count state ( K , C , J ) (K,C,J) . 3. Exact Count Propagation: Starting from initial count distribution μ 0 \mu_{0} , convolving the three source counts produces transfer matrix P ^ t \widehat{P}_{t} (heatmap: darker teal indicates higher probability). Over six rounds, core counts shift from t = 0 t=0 (dashed grey) leftward to t = 6 t=6 (solid plum, shaded failure tail), giving terminal risk R ^ \widehat{R} (Theorems 1 – 2 ). 4. Frozen Boundary Validation: The predicted 20% risk map (2-D DDPM, Fig. 4 c; colorbar shows risk %) is locked before running 192–576 independent chains. Bottom bars test Fashion-MNIST ( p = 20 % p=20\% , σ = 0.75 \sigma=0.75 ) at m ∈ { 72,112 } m\in\{72,112\} , whose joint 95% intervals bracket the dotted 20% line (Proposition 4 ).

2611.30962.image_caption: Figure 3 : System overview. CUA-SEE forms a closed loop of task evolution, verifier evolution, and agent-environment rollout, as summarized by the central workflow. The left panel details task evolution: rollout evidence is first aggregated at the batch level to plan the next round, followed by two complementary forms of per-task evolution: benchmark evolution for population-level measurement growth and diagnostic evolution for agent-conditional boundary refinement. The right panel presents verifier evolution, which progressively translates evolved task requirements into grounded, executable, and rigorously validated measurements. The bottom panel shows the shared substrate that supports all stages of the evaluation loop, expanding the 8 OSWorld applications to 20 verifiable desktop environments.

2611.31228.image_caption: Figure 1: Confidence Dynamics at the First Error Step ( k ∗ k^{*} ). Mean on-track confidence ( g k g_{k} , red circle) and step confidence ( c k c_{k} , blue square) centered at the earliest error step ( k − k ∗ = 0 k-k^{*}=0 ) with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals across four models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct , Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct , Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 , and Phi-4 (14.7B). Sample sizes at relative steps k − k ∗ < 0 k-k^{*}<0 exclude step-1 errors ( k ∗ = 1 k^{*}=1 , leaving n = 429 n=429 Qwen, 551 551 Llama, 646 646 Mistral, and 57 57 Phi-4 at k − k ∗ = − 1 k-k^{*}=-1 ). Trajectories remain flatly saturated at 95–100% across reasoning errors.
